A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, appendices, equations, figures and tables are readable and support a reliable comparison despite substantial expansion in v3.

before.justification: v1 reports original transformer-training results, linear-probing experiments and causal interventions on the small transformer and Mistral-7B.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds circuit-sufficiency tests, further probing controls and experiments on Gemma-2-9B.

M1.justification: The circuit-analysis methodology gains a substantial verification stage. Beyond v1's component-level necessity patching, v3 tests whole circuits by freezing non-circuit attention-head activations while allowing the selected circuit to process altered queries (Sections 4.2–4.3.2 and Appendix C.2). The trained solver architecture, objectives and ordinary inference remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic propositional-logic coverage: length-3 linear and AND/OR chains for small transformers, and restricted length-2 linear/OR problems for pretrained LLMs. Gemma and the additional interventions use this retained task coverage.

E2.justification: The model-size comparison retains the same candidates in v1 Figure 7 and v3 Figure 6. Gemma is another subject of mechanistic analysis, not a competing solution method. The new empty-circuit and head-family-removal conditions are experimental controls and ablations; no alternative solver or circuit-discovery baseline is introduced.

E3.justification: v3 adds circuit-level freezing, empty-circuit controls, head-family removals and a circuit logit-difference ratio. Gemma uses four in-context examples, while Mistral retains six; Gemma verification also patches a broader QUERY-to-colon token range. Additional negative-control probes change prediction targets and examine multiple layers and positions. These are new evaluation protocols, not evidence that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds sufficiency and head-family-removal tests for both LLMs, extensive Gemma circuit analysis, and probes testing whether the unqueried chain's answer is linearly accessible. Rule-location interventions expand to OR queries in Figure 17. Conversely, v1's coarse residual-stream and attention-block patching analysis, including its layer-transition finding, is omitted.

E5.justification: Both versions report three initialization seeds for the selected small architecture, three experiment sets for the LogOp-patching result, and standard deviations for attention statistics. The stated 60-sample default and 200-sample rule-location experiment are retained. Gemma plots extend the existing reporting practice; no new uncertainty-estimation procedure or explicit increase in repetitions is reported.

E6.justification: New results include circuit logit-difference ratios of 0.98 for Mistral and 0.94 for Gemma under their respective protocols, with family-removal results in Tables 1–2. Negative-control probes report approximately 27% and 32.7% test accuracy. The inferred Mistral circuit also gains mover head (13,22) and a fact-processing role for (14,26). Original Mistral accuracies of 96% for linear queries and 70% for OR queries remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 4.3.2 introduces an operational mathematical criterion for circuit sufficiency: the ratio of mean circuit-intervened logit difference to the unmodified altered-prompt logit difference. This extends v1's component-level metric definitions. No theorem or proof is added; the expanded transformer equations in Appendix B.2 primarily explain the existing architecture.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion expand from necessary components in Mistral to necessity-and-sufficiency evidence for circuits in both Mistral and Gemma. v3 adds claims of similar, human-like latent reasoning strategies and an explicit first-characterization novelty claim. The small-transformer routing contribution is retained.

C2.justification: v3 introduces potential circuit universality while cautioning that similar attention patterns do not establish equivalent functions or interactions. It explains the restriction to QUERY-sensitive reasoning, why MLPs remain active during verification, and why removing lower-level processing can invalidate a sufficiency test. Appendix C.7 additionally identifies the Gemma analysis as preliminary and limited by computation budget.

D1.justification: v3 supplies explicit circuit head sets, token-specific intervention locations, freezing rules and MLP treatment, including the additional position used for Mistral head (14,24) and Gemma's broader patching range. Appendix B.2 expands architectural documentation. Existing training hyperparameters, sample counts, V100 hardware and training-time information are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds references including Geiger et al., Marks et al., Merullo's Talking Heads, and the Mistral and Gemma model papers, while removing Brinkmann et al. (2024). It sharpens circuit-based positioning and adds an explicit novelty claim about latent multistep reasoning in pretrained LLMs. The main related-work categories remain the same.

P1.justification: The introduction and contribution framing are substantially rewritten. Section 3 combines the chain-answer discussions, and Section 4 is reorganized around discovery, verification and deeper examinations. Extensive architecture and intervention explanations are added in the appendices, substantially changing the exposition beyond the added experimental content.

P2.justification: v3 adds architecture, reasoning-flow and intervention diagrams, five Gemma figures and two sufficiency tables. Main-text patching displays are reorganized, group-patching results move to Appendix Figure 12, and the rule-location figure gains linear/OR panels. The original coarse patching figure is removed, while retained figures are relocated or expanded.

improvement.justification: v1 primarily establishes that individual components influence reasoning. v3 substantially strengthens their joint causal explanation through circuit-sufficiency tests and head-family removals (Tables 1–2), supported by negative-control probes and a second pretrained model. The added procedural explanations and explicit limits on sufficiency and cross-model similarity improve assessability. Although the coarse patching analysis is removed and Gemma evidence remains preliminary, the new validation addresses an important gap in the original circuit account.
